data.text: Lusaka's council budgeted K63.4m in levies for 2026, about K174,000 a day. If the 8,000 moved vendors took K50–K100 a day each, that's K400,000–K800,000 a day in takings. How much of it survives the move from pavement to market stall? #econsky

For more than five years, Maxwell Mwenda traded from a makeshift shop on Lumumba Road. When Lusaka's 29 September deadline passed, he pulled it down himself. Will he still be trading, legally and profitably, a year from now? #econsky

More than 8,000 vendors have been moved out of Lusaka's city centre under Operation Clear Path. Lusaka cleared its pavements in 2018; by October 2019 vending had formally resumed on Lumumba Road. Is the problem the vendor, or the plan? #econsky
Before Zambia makes transformers for the world, its own grid needs a $12bn overhaul. Should Zambia fix power first, or build the factories that would force the fix? #econsky
Zambia holds about 4% of the copper market. Is the faster route to 8% more mines, or factories that turn Zambian copper into products? #econsky

Zambia wants copper to do for it what oil did for the Middle East. But copper is a ~$385bn market and oil is $6–8tn. Can Zambia grow the market, or does it have to win a bigger share of a small one? #econsky
